label: SUPPLY_EDGE_2: a supply edge whose supplier guarantees the recipient
definition: SUPPLY_EDGE_2, on the modal-covariation proxy. Intended ordinary meaning: an actual supplier whose presence by itself selects the recipient's existence. The proxy over the #505 Profile (SufficientSupply m w y x): y exists at w, m.grounds w y x, and at every world accessible from w at which y exists, x exists. Example (formal): the realization rule 'L implies a and b' of the mixed rival in docs/notes/direct-grounding-warrant.md, which selects the positive assignment. Limit (mis-sorted case): the proxy also counts as SUPPLY_EDGE_2 every edge into a recipient that exists wherever its supplier exists, including every edge into a NECESSARY_2 recipient, even when the supplier is only one partial contributor among several; an edge in this sense therefore does not show that the supplier suffices. Non-example: an equality constraint between recipients (SUPPLY_EDGE_1). Strict implication records modal covariation, not how the supplier selects existence; it is not efficient production and gives no account of supplying esse. Distinguished from the neutral Profile edge and from a complete cause (DISAMB-COMPLETE-CAUSE-PARTIAL-GROUND).
note: Analyst sense introduced in the #1553 challenge repair, attribution deferred. Under CONCRETE_6, a nonconcrete sufficient supplier of esse owes an account of how what has no esse in re gives esse (docs/notes/esse-root-leaves.md, section (f) row 6); this definition records the reading, not that account. Whether accessible worlds represent the relevant existence alternatives is an OPEN application obligation.
